text:
alex: Heads-up: running into a mess with rate-limit headers from hosted endpoints when using the Python SDK. Different services return different header names and formats and it's causing flaky client-side retry logic.

alex: Examples I've observed in production logs: 
```
Retry-After: 120
retry-after: Wed, 01 Apr 2026 12:00:00 GMT
x-ratelimit-reset: 1715000000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
RateLimit-Remaining: 0
x-rl-reset-in: 30
x-ratelimit-limit: 100/3600
```

nora: Ugh. We should standardize parsing in the SDK rather than rely on callers. Proposal: add two helper APIs: `parse_retry_after(header: Optional[str]) -> Optional[float]` (seconds until retry) and `parse_ratelimit_headers(headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> RateLimitInfo`. `RateLimitInfo` should be a simple frozen dataclass with fields `limit: Optional[int]`, `remaining: Optional[int]`, `reset_at: Optional[float]` (epoch seconds), and `raw: Dict[str, str]`.

ryan: +1. For `parse_retry_after` follow RFC7231: accept integer seconds or an HTTP-date. Implementation notes: treat negative numbers as 0, cap huge values to a safe max (e.g., 7 days) to avoid sleeping forever. Add unit tests for malformed values like "-5", "9999999999999", and non-ASCII whitespace.

kevin: For header name normalization, do case-insensitive lookup and accept common vendor keys: `retry-after`, `x-retry-after`, `x-ratelimit-reset`, `x-rl-reset`, `x-ratelimit-reset-in`. When `x-ratelimit-reset` is numeric it may be either epoch seconds OR seconds-until-reset, so detect heuristically (if value > 10**10 treat as epoch).

alex: Another practical request: return both `reset_at` as epoch seconds and `reset_in` as seconds-until-reset in RateLimitInfo (both optional) so callers can log whichever is more convenient. Also include the original raw header map so teams can log vendor-specific keys.

nora: Async ergonomics: many apps call the API at high concurrency and need client-side rate limiting. We have a tiny sync token-bucket in `tools/ratelimit.py` but nothing async. I propose `redwood.utils.throttle.AsyncTokenBucket` supporting `async with limiter.acquire(perm=1):` semantics and a non-blocking `try_acquire()` which returns False immediately. Implementation sketch in docstring is fine for PR.

ryan: Important: users expect the SDK's `auto_retry` feature to honor `Retry-After` (when present) and override exponential-backoff delays. Suggest `ClientConfig.auto_retry: bool`, `auto_retry_strategy: Optional[str]` with choices "retry-after-aware" or "standard-expo". Default should be conservative (expo) and opt-in for `retry-after-aware`.

kevin: One gotcha: streaming endpoints (chunked SSE or websocket-style) should never be retried by waiting on Retry-After in the middle of a stream. The SDK should only apply `auto_retry` on top-level request failures (no active stream). Document that clearly.

alex: Small typing note for mypy: callers currently do `headers.get("Retry-After")` which yields `Optional[str]`. The helper should accept `Optional[str]` and return `Optional[float]` (seconds). For `parse_ratelimit_headers` accept `Mapping[str, str]` and return `RateLimitInfo`. This keeps annotations simple.

nora: devx-bot opened https://git.internal/infra/issues/5120 for this work and linked a spike doc. Assigning to @devex. Please add an example file `examples/async_rate_limit_demo.py` showing: parse headers, build RateLimitInfo, use AsyncTokenBucket to gate requests, handle Retry-After in backoff.

devx-bot: Created issue #5120: "py-sdk: ratelimit header normalization + async token-bucket + typed helpers" — assigned to @devex.

ryan: I'll take the typed helpers + tests (mypy & pytest). I'll include edge-case fixtures with different header variants.

kevin: I'll own the AsyncTokenBucket implementation and the example. I'll make it cancellable-friendly (support `asyncio.TimeoutError` flow) and include a sync wrapper.

alex: Thanks — one last ask: add observability hooks so callers can opt into a callback when we parse headers (for metrics/alerting). Maybe `ClientConfig.on_ratelimit(headers)` optional callback.

nora: Good idea. Log the raw map + parsed RateLimitInfo in the callback.

alex: Great. I'll draft a short RFC PR with proposed function signatures and the dataclass shape. Ping reviewers when it's ready.

kevin: I'll land the example + implementation after the RFC lands.

devx-bot: Linked RFC PR #789 and the issue.
